The Minister of Solid Minerals Development, Dele Alake, has defended President Bola Tinubu’s economic reforms, arguing that the policies are necessary to lay the foundation for long-term economic prosperity.
Mr Alake, who is also the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Spokesperson, said the ruling party would focus on issues and its record in government during the 2027 general election campaign, rather than engage in political violence or distractions.
The minister spoke during an interview on TVC News’ Politics Tonight, where he discussed the administration’s economic policies, the restructuring of the APC Presidential Campaign Council’s media team and criticisms from opposition politicians.
He described the decision to restrict the number of authorised campaign spokespersons to three as an administrative measure designed to improve coordination and ensure consistency in the party’s public communication.
According to him, the decision was not intended to diminish the status of those previously appointed as spokespersons.
“It was an administrative decision to ensure synergy in messaging and prevent coordination issues. It was not about loss of status for previous members,” he said.
On reports of political violence and the use of weapons at campaign rallies, Mr Alake insisted that the APC was committed to an issue-based campaign.

He accused opposition supporters of orchestrating acts of violence and using social media to create misleading narratives about the ruling party.
He said the APC would concentrate on its policies and achievements, arguing that opposition parties resorted to distractions because they lacked credible alternatives to the administration’s programmes.
The minister also defended the removal of petrol subsidy and the unification of the foreign exchange market, describing both policies as necessary to address longstanding distortions in the economy.
He argued that the former subsidy regime encouraged fuel smuggling and allowed individuals to benefit from government-subsidised petrol at the expense of the country.
He also said the previous multiple exchange rate system created opportunities for individuals with connections at the Central Bank of Nigeria to profit from preferential access to foreign exchange.
Mr Alake said the reforms improved foreign exchange liquidity and the ability of businesses, particularly international airlines, to repatriate their earnings.
He cited the clearance of a $7 billion backlog of trapped airline funds as evidence of improved access to foreign exchange. He also attributed an increase in non-oil exports to the depreciation of the naira.
Acknowledging the hardship associated with the reforms, the minister described the current economic difficulties as temporary adjustments necessary to address deeper structural problems.
He said savings from the removal of petrol subsidy were being redirected to agriculture, manufacturing and industrial development.
Mr Alake also claimed that the measures had helped reduce inflation from 34 per cent to 14 per cent and increased Nigeria’s foreign reserves from $3 billion to $46 billion within three years.
He further argued that the removal of the subsidy had improved the finances of state governments, allowing administrations that previously struggled to pay workers’ salaries to meet their obligations.
Mr Alake also dismissed criticisms of the Tinubu administration by opposition politicians, including former Minister of Transportation Rotimi Amaechi, who has accused the government of worsening corruption.
He questioned the records of opposition figures who had previously held public office, arguing that their criticisms should be measured against their own achievements in government.
He challenged former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar and former Anambra State Governor Peter Obi to identify major legacy projects from their respective tenures.
“What legacy projects survived from Atiku Abubakar’s term as vice-president or Peter Obi’s term as governor of Anambra?” he asked.
The minister also cited projects such as Eko Atlantic and Awolowo Road in Lagos as examples of Mr Tinubu’s record as governor of the state, arguing that his performance demonstrated his capacity for effective leadership.
Mr Alake also highlighted the performance of the Ministry of Solid Minerals Development, attributing improvements in revenue generation to the Tinubu administration’s economic diversification agenda.
He said the ministry generated ₦6 billion in revenue, which he attributed to efforts to revitalise the solid minerals sector and implement the administration’s Renewed Hope Agenda.
He said the government was pursuing economic diversification by strengthening the mining sector and improving its contribution to national revenue.
